options: A row per step (plus a summary row) for every job run Agent actually attempted
Every T-SQL query ever run on the server
Only successful job runs, never failures
The list of all jobs that currently exist, regardless of whether they've run
questions.explain: sysjobhistory records execution history — but only for runs Agent actually attempted; a job that never started leaves no row there.

questions.q: A job has zero rows in sysjobhistory since it was created. Where should you look next, per this lesson?
options: Whether the Agent service is running, and whether the job or its schedule is disabled
sysjobhistory again, since the answer must be there somewhere
The SQL Server Database Engine's error log exclusively
The linked server configuration
questions.explain: A total absence of history rows points to Agent never attempting the run — the Agent service being stopped, or a disabled job/schedule, or missing server targeting.

questions.q: Where is SQL Server Agent's error log, relative to the Database Engine's error log?
options: It's a separate log file, viewable in SSMS under SQL Server Agent > Error Logs
They are the exact same file
Agent has no error log of its own
It's stored only in the Windows System event log, never in SSMS
questions.explain: Agent maintains its own separate error log from the Database Engine's, logging service start/stop and schedule engine activity.

questions.q: A CmdExec step's sysjobhistory message shows 'Access is denied.' What does this most strongly suggest?
options: The step is likely running under the wrong Windows identity — a proxy/credential permission issue
The T-SQL syntax in the step has a typo
The job's schedule is disabled
SQL Server Agent itself is not installed
questions.explain: An access-denied message on a CmdExec step points back to the identity the step runs under — a missing or misconfigured proxy is the classic cause.

questions.q: Why does a proxy permission failure behave differently, diagnostically, than the Agent service being stopped?
options: A proxy failure still leaves a row in sysjobhistory with a specific error message, while a stopped Agent service leaves no row at all
They behave identically in every respect
A proxy failure never appears in any log
A stopped Agent service always leaves a detailed error message in sysjobhistory
questions.explain: Because Agent actually attempted the run before the proxy failed, sysjobhistory gets a row; a stopped Agent service means no attempt was ever made, so there's no row to inspect.
